newsitem.title: USA: Brent talk fades on US Gulf Coast, arb narrows.
newsitem.headline: Brent talk fades on US Gulf Coast, arb narrows.

text.p: A narrowing transatlantic arbitrage and stronger quotes for dated Brent in Europe diminished talk of bringing the North Sea benchmark to the U.S. Gulf Coast on Wednesday, traders said.
A U.S. company was still offering the last Brent cargo off a VLCC loading around May 10, asking 77 cents under West Texas Intermediate/Cushing on a delivered basis.
One cargo was already sold to a Gulf Coast refiner for a discount of 80 cents to WTI.
The seller was expected to keep two more of the cargoes for its own refining system.
Among other North Sea grades, a pair of Norwegian Oseberg cargoes were still available for mid-May arrival at WTI minus 70 cents a barrel delivered.
The same seller was offering Troll for June 1-5 at WTI minus 60 cents a barrel, traders said.
The June spread between WTI and Brent was around $1.65-70 a barrel Wednesday afternoon, down about five cents from late Tuesday.
Meanwhile, two dated Brent cargoes were sold at June Brent minus 27 cents, up two cents from Tuesday's dealings, undercutting the incentive to bring barrels to the Gulf Coast, traders said.
Among West Africa pickings, a U.S. company was offering a Brass River for June 5-10 arrival, asking dated Brent plus $2.05 delivered, traders said.
In Latin America, Colombia's state oil company Ecopetrol was tendering to sell four crude cargoes loading in June, trade sources said.
Two Cusiana cargoes were available for loading June 3-7 and June 5-9.
One Cano Limon was available for loading June 13-23.
Finally, one South Blend cargo was on offer for loading June 20-30.
